subject: Re: Deployment model follow-up — Dedicated vs Private VPC (data isolation)
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>

Subject: Deployment model follow-up — Dedicated vs Private VPC (data isolation)

Hi Tom —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and the next steps I promised:

Summary of customer's stated needs
- Primary requirement: strong data isolation for customer PII/PHI + auditability for regulators.
- Preference to keep model inference off shared multi-tenant control planes where possible.
- Concern: key management (KMS/HSM) and ability to provide customer-managed KMS and audit logs.

Options we discussed (high level)
1) Hosted API — fastest to deploy, but runs on Redwood shared hosted environment; not ideal for regulated PHI workloads unless combined with strong contractual controls and data access agreements.
2) Dedicated — reserved GPU pools for the customer; provides tenant isolation for serving but still uses Redwood control plane. Good middle ground for predictable throughput and isolation of inference workloads.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem) — full network isolation, customer-managed control plane or on-prem package; recommended when customer needs to control KMS/HSM and networking for compliance.

Follow-ups / Asks
- Can you confirm whether FinSecure requires customer-owned KMS/HSM, or whether tenant-specific KMS within the cloud provider is sufficient?
- Is there a hard requirement for on-prem (air-gapped) vs VPC-only?
- Would regulatory auditors require direct access to our audit logs, or are exported, signed logs sufficient?

Next steps
- I attached a short one-pager that compares Dedicated vs Private VPC (redwood-dedicated-vs-private-vpc-one-pager.pdf).
- If you confirm the KMS/networking requirement, we can schedule a technical deep-dive with marissa (solutions engineering) and rachel (security) next week.
- I'll also put together a MAP (mutual action plan) if you're comfortable — I attached a draft.

Thanks — available for a quick sync if helpful.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez

Subject: Re: Deployment model follow-up — Dedicated vs Private VPC (data isolation)

Mateo —

Thanks for the recap and the one-pager. A few clarifications from our side:

- KMS: we need customer-managed keys. Hosted customer-managed KMS (customer keys in cloud KMS, but access managed by Redwood) might be OK, but ideally keys are under our control (bring-your-own-KMS) and we can rotate them.
- Network: VPC with strict peering and airflow controls is acceptable. On-prem (air-gapped) would be a last resort due to cost and timeline, but we need to know the option is supported.
- Audit logs: exported, signed audit logs are acceptable. For SOC/Praxis reviews our auditors will want a way to validate no cross-tenant data access.

Timeline: we're aiming for a pilot in Q3; procurement will need an initial SOW and some security artifacts (SOC2 report, data flow diagrams, KMS diagrams). Can you confirm Redwood can provide SOC2 and an architecture diagram showing separation at the serving/runtime layer?

Also: any rough order of magnitude for Dedicated vs Private (on-prem) in terms of monthly run cost for a pilot-sized footprint (say, 4 GPUs)? Ballpark is fine.

Thanks — Tom
Tom Bartlett
Head of Cloud Security | FinSecure
tom.bartlett@finsecure.com

Tom —

Appreciate the clear asks. Quick answers inline and proposed next steps below.

KMS
- We support customer-managed KMS in two forms: (1) cloud KMS where the customer owns the keys and grants Redwood a limited role to use them for inference, and (2) customer-hosted HSMs for Private/on-prem installs. For strict custody requirements we recommend the Private deployment so that key material never leaves customer control.

Network / VPC vs On-prem
- VPC: Redwood Private (VPC) provides a customer-managed VPC peering model and private control plane connectivity. Serving nodes are in the customer's VPC; control plane can be private or routed over an encrypted management channel. This covers most regulated use cases and preserves operational speed.
- On-prem: supported via our on-prem package. We can run inference and control plane components in your environment for an air-gapped option; this requires additional engineering time and a separate license line item.

Audit logs
- We can provide exported, signed audit logs and per-request tracing that shows model, route, and token-level PSD/TX traces for compliance review. Rachel can share a sample log export format.

Rough costs (ballpark for pilot, 4 GPUs)
- Dedicated (reserved): ~$18k-25k / month depending on GPU type and commitment length.
- Private (VPC): ~$25k-35k / month estimate for a managed VPC deployment; on-prem air-gapped will be higher due to installation and support (~one-time onboarding + higher monthly license). We'll provide firm pricing in an SOW.

Next steps
1) I'll pull together the SOC2 artifacts and an architecture sketch.
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Marissa (solutions engineering) and Rachel (security) — can we do Tue or Wed next week? Please propose times.
3) I attached a draft MAP (MAP-FinSecure-20270418.pdf) with milestones for security review and pilot.

Let me know which time works and we'll lock it.

Tom —

Quick technical notes ahead of the deep-dive:

- Separation at runtime: Dedicated provides tenant-level isolation for inference (separate GPU pools and namespaces). KV cache and model artifacts are isolated per-tenant; we run per-tenant processes.
- Control plane: in Dedicated the control plane is still Redwood-managed but can be configured with strict RBAC and encrypted channels. In Private/VPC we can either run a customer-managed control plane or a managed control plane with private connectivity — for the highest assurance run a customer-managed control plane.
- KMS integration: For VPC deployments we support Cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault) with customer keys. For on-prem we support HSM integrations and BYOK flows.
- Evidence: I'll bring sample network diagrams (VPC peering, flow of request, where keys live) and a sanitized audit log sample to the call.

Proposed times for the tech deep-dive (PST): Tue 4/20 10:00-11:00, Tue 4/20 15:00-16:00, Wed 4/21 09:00-10:00. Pick one and I'll send a calendar invite with an agenda.

Thanks — looking forward.

Marissa Cole
